Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2025 (published July 23, 2025), Raymond James described private-equity-backed roll-ups as a relatively novel and aggressive competitive dynamic in advisor recruiting: “The dynamic that’s relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), Raymond James contrasted itself with competitors that compete with the largest check and change their compensation plans each year to cross-sell more bank products, saying: “many of our competitors compete with the largest check.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2024 (published January 29, 2025), Raymond James said the departure of primarily one large branch in its Independent Contractor Division impacted net new assets by approximately $5 billion of assets under administration: “the departure of primarily one large branch in our Independent Contractor Division. The impact was approximately $5 billion of AUA.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended December 31, 2024 (published January 29, 2025), Raymond James said it has historically had about 1% regretted attrition, and that the biggest movement of people to the RIA channel has gone to its own RIA so the firm kept the assets: “We’ve historically had that 1% type of regretted attrition, but we don’t see anything big on the leaving side. The biggest movement of people that have gone to RIA, fortunately, have gone to our RIA, so we’ve kept the assets.”

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025 (published October 22, 2025), Raymond James said it expects to lose a platform of about $2.7 billion of assets through bank M&A: “From time to time with bank M&A, next quarter, for example, there’ll be a platform that we’ll lose just through bank M&A. I think it’s a $2.7 billion of assets.”
